textBlocks.text: As You Go through Your Day, Don’t Forget! Though there are siddurim that list just four, and some list ten, this list of six “remembrances” is the most common custom. Note that there are three positive elements to focus on: Hashem redeemed us from Egypt (and will in the future); Hashem spoke directly to us at Har Sinai (which obligates us); and Shabbos, which reminds us of Creation (and thus His providence). The three negative elements tell us to always be on guard about: the Golden Calf (sins against Hashem); Miriam’s lashon hara (sins against others); and Amalek (nations who do not fear Hashem, no matter how seemingly “cultured,” can act with great cruelty). The point is not to mumble them like some magic formula! Rather, the idea is to focus on these key points and use them as your guide during your day.
We must remember that Hashem took us out of Egypt with great miracles, which gives us hope that He will again redeem us and take us out of this final galus!
We must remember the unique defining moment of Bnei Yisrael, when Hashem spoke to three million of us at Har Sinai, and gave us His Torah.
We must remember the evil of Amalek attacking us for no reason right after the miracle of the splitting of the sea. We are obligated to wipe out evil!
We must remember how we angered Hashem when we attempted to serve Him our own way, rather than as prescribed by His Torah, notwithstanding all our good intentions!
We must remember what Hashem did to Miriam: Her punishment for speaking lashon hara about Moshe, even though it was a seemingly minor
